subject: Staged pin shelving & evacuation guidelines for May maintenance
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@vantanbank.com>, Ben Thomas <ben.thomas@vantanbank.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staged pin shelving & evacuation guidelines for May maintenance

Hi Lena / Ben —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Attached is our proposed staging plan (pin_schedule_v2.xlsx) and the current VPC/network diagram for the private deployment. High level ask: we want to perform a staggered pin-shelving of the Redwood Private control plane and inference runtime across three racks in your DC on May 19th, with a compact rollback window in case we observe service regressions.

Quick overview: 
- Goal: apply runtime micropatches + kernel hotfix with minimal surface area.
- Approach: staggered 3-stage pin-shelving (rack A -> rack B -> rack C). Each rack will be drained, patched, validated, then unpinned.
- Expected outage: no more than 3-5s tail latency spikes per pod during KV cache warm-up if rollback not needed.

We need two confirmations from your side: 
1) Blackout windows (no scheduled batch jobs) — please confirm the safe 4-hour window on May 19th you propose in the sheet.
2) ACL & firewall changes — we'll need a short temporary allowlist for our patching orchestrator (IPs listed in the CSV) and a port 22 maintenance allowance from Redwood ops for 30 minutes per rack.

Rollback triggers we propose (we'll control these from the shiproom):
- >= 10% error rate increase on /generate endpoints for > 5 minutes
- sustained 20% request latency degradation (p50->p95 delta) for > 10 minutes
- KV cache corruption detected during canonical checks

Please find the attachments and add any operational constraints we should bake into the runbook.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pin_schedule_v2.xlsx, vpc-network-diagram.pdf
From: Lena Park <lena.park@vantanbank.com>

Cc: Ben Thomas <ben.thomas@vantanbank.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Staged pin shelving & evacuation guidelines for May maintenance

Hi Ava —

Appreciate the clear plan. A couple of notes from our side after reviewing the sheet: 
- Blackout window: we can confirm a primary window 2027-05-19 01:00-05:00 UTC (our peak is outside that slot). Please avoid 03:00-03:30 UTC due to an internal settlement batch.
- Firewall/ACL: Ben will schedule the temporary allowlist change and we can open SSH from your orchestrator IPs for 30 minutes per rack as requested. See attached firewall-rule-matrix.csv — I added the internal VLAN IDs you should reference.
- Observability: we need an explicit telemetry spike threshold for p95 rather than p50 — p95 + 15% sustained for 5 minutes should require an immediate hold.

One operational constraint: our compliance team requires that any rollback that reverts to a pinned older runtime include a security re-scan report within 24 hours. If you need us to run that, flag it in the postmortem.

I'll loop in cloud-ops@thirdparty.net for the ACL change window.

Best,
Lena Park
Platform Ops Lead, VantanBank
lena.park@vantanbank.com

Attachment: firewall-rule-matrix.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Lena Park <lena.park@vantanbank.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Staged pin shelving & evacuation guidelines for May maintenance

Thanks Lena — noted on the p95 threshold and the security-scan requirement. A few technical clarifications / asks from the shiproom side so we have deterministic rollback behavior: 

Pre-patch checklist (what we will do):
- KV-cache snapshot and checkpoint to S3-compatible object store (retention: 72h).
- Graceful connection drain: 30s drain, then cut new connections for the node.
- Canary: enable 2% traffic canary to patched rack for 10 minutes; run synthetic prompt set and golden evaluation (we will push results to the runbook URL).

Rollback automation & triggers: 
- Automatic rollback if (a) p95 + 15% sustained for 5 consecutive minutes OR (b) error rate spike >= 10% for 5 consecutive minutes OR (c) any KV integrity check fails.
- Rollback steps: 1) immediately stop dispatching to patched nodes; 2) bootstrap previous pinned image and restore KV checkpoint; 3) validate health checks for 10 minutes; 4) mark rollback event in audit log and notify Vantan ops.

Escalation matrix (brief):
- Stage lead (Karthik) -> Engineering on-call -> Ava (SE) -> Lena (Vantan ops).

Question for Vantan: do you have a pre-approved maintenance exception for brief SSH access from external orchestrator IPs, or should we run the entire patch using a jumpbox inside your DMZ? If exception is not allowed we will adapt to jumpbox flow.

I'll add a short thermostat to the runbook so we don't kick a rollback on transient single-minute spikes.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
